question:
After each change to a system, how should the team decide what to test again, and at which point of the process?

Answer with a list of guidelines. After each guideline, cite the source it comes from: the path of the SWEBOK file if you have it, otherwise a verbatim quote of at least 8 words from the passage, in the form (source: ...).

# Guidelines
- Define regression testing as the selective retesting of the system under test ([SWEBOK excerpt e1d8960115ee098d2d93]. The goal is to show the SUT still passes previously passed tests. (source: root/Software Testing Levels, Objectives, and Approaches/Alpha, Beta, and Regression Testing Procedures.md) [JEV 0.98]
- Conduct regression testing at every test level (unit, integration, system, etc.), not only at the end of the process, since [SWEBOK excerpt 3fabf7234e69eb7aaa75]. (source: root/Software Testing Levels, Objectives, and Approaches/Alpha, Beta, and Regression Testing Procedures.md) [JEV 0.92]
- Apply test selection and minimization techniques when deciding what to re-test: use test-case selection (choosing a relevant subset) and test-suite minimization (reducing redundant tests), combined with prioritization approaches, to manage the cost of regression testing after a change. (source: root/Software Testing Levels, Objectives, and Approaches/Regression Testing in Software Development.md) [JEV 0.95]
- Perform regression testing [SWEBOK excerpt 54698dde064ed8064539]. It [SWEBOK excerpt 809dded00b7e008c7e11]. (source: root/Software Testing Levels, Objectives, and Approaches/Regression Testing in Software Development.md) [JEV 0.98]
- Cover both functional and non-functional properties in regression testing after a change — including [SWEBOK excerpt 6081dd06be3ad080f185] — not just functional correctness. (source: root/Software Testing Levels, Objectives, and Approaches/Regression Testing in Software Development.md) [JEV 0.94]
- Prioritize [SWEBOK excerpt dd8bd0bb133cd433eedf] after a change. Test case prioritization schedules tests to increase code coverage and SUT reliability; [SWEBOK excerpt 526de9ba5a2fa5a5b414] heuristics. (source: root/Software Testing Levels, Objectives, and Approaches/Test Case Prioritization for Fault Detection.md) [JEV 0.96]
- Make a deliberate trade-off between the assurance provided by running every regression test after each change and the resources required. Because regression suites can be very large, the team should weigh the cost of full re-execution against the risk of skipping tests. (source: root/Software Testing Levels, Objectives, and Approaches/Alpha, Beta, and Regression Testing Procedures.md) [JEV 0.97]
- Automate regression testing as part of a Continuous Integration (CI) pipeline so that each integration of a change triggers an automated build and test run, detecting integration errors as quickly as possible. (source: root/Software Maintenance and Configuration Management/Software Maintenance, Evolution, and Quality Assurance/Continuous Integration, Delivery, and Software Maintenance/Continuous Integration and DevOps Practices/Continuous Integration, Delivery, Testing and Deployment.md) [JEV 0.97]
- Adopt continuous testing — testing [SWEBOK excerpt a3bf4affce14a7425dbf] — to evaluate software quality at every step of the [SWEBOK excerpt d7e57d9d89af6c96b337]. (source: root/Software Maintenance and Configuration Management/Software Maintenance, Evolution, and Quality Assurance/Continuous Integration, Delivery, and Software Maintenance/Continuous Delivery and Testing in Software Development.md) [JEV 0.97]
- Make CI's fundamental goal the automatic catching of [SWEBOK excerpt 11b16f70a3b614b71ba9] the [SWEBOK excerpt 796ed381ef76f96ebd07], automating [SWEBOK excerpt a853e65b19742ecda354]. (source: root/Software Maintenance and Configuration Management/Software Maintenance, Evolution, and Quality Assurance/Continuous Integration, Delivery, and Software Maintenance/Continuous Integration and DevOps Practices/Continuous Integration Goals and Automated Processes.md) [JEV 0.97]
- Promote the shift-left testing movement: adopt [SWEBOK excerpt a893583528935d04e4d4], increasing overall SUT quality and reducing cost and risks. (source: root/Software Testing, Operations, and Maintenance/Testing Across Development Processes and Domains/Unified Process Phases and Shift-Left Testing Movement.md) [JEV 0.98]
- In Agile processes, manage the risk of regression defects explicitly as an objective of the testing process, including managing the impact of changing requirements on test artifacts. (source: root/Software Testing, Operations, and Maintenance/Testing Across Development Processes and Domains/Testing Strategies Across Methodologies and Domains/Testing Techniques Across Development Levels and Shift-Left Approaches.md) [JEV 0.97]
- Design the test process to allow automation of different testing phases and rely on [SWEBOK excerpt fb7953704b625fa5aa98], applicable to all life cycle models. (source: root/Testing Methodologies and Quality Assurance Practices/Software Testing Techniques, Measurement, and Management/Test Effectiveness and Process Levels/Software Testing Process Levels and Practical Considerations.md) [JEV 0.97]
- Leverage test case reusability to reduce the cost and effort of re-testing after changes. [SWEBOK excerpt 24059ee976fc27295ceb], and also improves test effectiveness. (source: root/Testing Methodologies and Quality Assurance Practices/Software Testing Techniques, Measurement, and Management/Test Planning and Reusability Strategy/Test Case Reusability in Software Development.md) [JEV 0.97]
